# Draft:Young Scots for Independence

Young Scots for Independence (also known as YSI) is the youth wing of the Scottish National Party (SNP), representing members aged 16-30 in Scotland. It was formed in the 1970s.
The YSI maintains autonomy from the SNP and as such is entitled to formulate its own policies and run its own campaigns.
The organisation has regional branches that correspond to the Scottish Parliament electoral regions
History
The organisation was formed in the 1970s. Key figures were Nicola Sturgeon and Shona Robison  who would both later become SNP members of the Scottish Parliament, with Sturgeon becoming First Minister of Scotland in 2014.
It has played an active part in the affairs of the SNP and is represented on the party's National Executive Committee, in the past with a representative position shared with SNP Students, but now each organisation has its own representative.
It has informal links with Plaid Ifanc, the youth wing of Plaid Cymru, and is also a part of the European Free Alliance Youth.
Activity
Young Scots for Independence has been very active in recent years, supporting high-profile campaigns such as the Tie Campaign, which support teaching young people about LGBT issues.
In 2012, during the SNP's policy change on NATO membership of an independent Scotland, Young Scots for Independence publicly came out in favour of retaining the anti-NATO policy, however at SNP conference the vote was lost despite YSI delegates voting against, and as a result the SNP is now pro-NATO. In 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the YSI voted for the organisation to support NATO membership, ending decades of opposition
Organisation
The organisation is run by a National Executive Committee (NEC) elected each year at the SNP Students' Annual Conference. The Committee currently comprises a Convener, Vice Convener, Secretary, Treasurer, Organiser, Equalities Officer, Women's Officer, Political Education Officer, and Communications Officer.
